newsitem.title: GERMANY: Yeltsin loves to cook, shares blame for chaos-wife.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin loves to cook, shares blame for chaos-wife.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has a heart of gold, hates untidiness and loves to cook, but shares the blame for the fact that millions of Russians' wages have not been paid, his wife says in a weekend interview.

In a rare public comment, Naina Yeltsina told Monday's edition of the German news weekly Der Spiegel that she did not have political ambitions, but that women would one day play a bigger part in the political life of her country.
Yeltsina also said her husband was "completely restored" after having heart bypass surgery late last year. "Boris Nikolayevich never spares himself," she said.
The president and his wife are due to visit Germany on Thursday, when he will meet his friend Chancellor Helmut Kohl before receiving a German media prize as Man of the Year.

Yeltsina said she had not lost touch with the problems of ordinary people, and that sometimes she cried because she could not do more to help. "My schoolfiends from Sverdlovsk often ring and pour their hearts out to me," she said.

Asked why the government could not even manage to make sure wages and pensions were paid, she replied: "There have to be guilty parties. The government and the President are responsible, there can be no doubt about that.

"But to say things would be better if the reforms had not been tackled -- that's wrong... Many people have forgotten how things used to be. Money was printed without a second thought to pay wages and pensions, but you couldn't buy anything for it."
Yeltsina said her husband had an "unbending will" to tackle Russia's problems.
"And he has intuition, he sees events coming. He knows what tomorrow will bring and so overcomes all obstacles. He is also an optimist, which makes life easier for all of us."
She said she and Yeltsin never fought, even when they had disagreements. "If you're not happy with the other, it doesn't have to mean a fight," she said. "He has a heart of gold."
Yeltsina said her husband was not above helping out in the household. "He's even glad to do it. He can't stand untidiness," she said, adding that Yeltsin also liked to cook.
"He does stuffed fish best, better than I do it."

The president's wife said women had an important political role in Russia in educating children in patriotism and loyalty to the state, but that it was also wrong to appoint state officials on the basis of gender.

"The main thing is that everyone should develop their own abilities and do something useful for humanity," she said. "Since women have no less brains than men, they will play a bigger role in politics one day, even in Russia," Yeltsina said.
